project: CLI BAD_REQUEST Classification and Honest Run Progress
description: Make you run classify customer invocation-argument mistakes as BAD_REQUEST failures and provide truthful non-JSON progress showing accepted work, dependency edges, active workers, and workstation/work details while preserving clean machine-readable modes.

context.customerAsk: Correct invocation-argument failures across the CLI surface so typos are reported as client errors, and add truthful you run progress showing active workers, accepted work and dependency edges, and workstation details with more useful color differentiation.
context.problem: Unknown or invalid Factory invocation arguments can be rendered as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, causing operators and agents to misdiagnose their own input. Human run output also hides generated work details, dependency edges, active worker state, and workstation/work associations, and its colors do not distinguish concurrent workers well.
context.solution: Classify customer-correctable invocation parse and validation failures at the CLI boundary as BAD_REQUEST while preserving stable codes and exit 1. Extend the human Factory Event projection with deterministic work/dependency and worker/workstation progress, gate animation and color through terminal policy, and regenerate the authored CLI manifest contract after rebasing.

acceptanceCriteria: Unknown and invalid invocation arguments across you run render one standard stderr error response with family BAD_REQUEST, retain the specific invocation error code, never claim INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, and exit with code 1.
A recorded non-JSON run rendering lists accepted work items with identifiers/descriptions and renders every available DEPENDS_ON edge in an unambiguous direction.
A recorded concurrent run rendering shows one status line per active worker and names each workstation together with associated work IDs when those IDs are present in canonical events.
Quiet, redirected/non-interactive, JSON, and NDJSON modes remain valid: no animation or ANSI bytes enter structured output, quiet suppresses progress, and redirected human output is deterministic.

contracts/cli/commands.json describes the resulting you run errors and output behavior; make cli-manifest-generate is run after rebasing, generated CLI manifests are never hand-merged, and every intentional golden diff is explained in the PR.

no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green; typecheck, focused CLI tests, CLI contract checks, and affected functional/golden tests pass.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Classify invocation mistakes as client errors
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want invalid invocation arguments identified as my request error so that I can correct the command instead of investigating a false server failure.
acceptanceCriteria: An unknown Factory invocation flag produces one stderr error response with its specific INVOCATION_ARGUMENT_* code and family BAD_REQUEST, not INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.

Missing values, positional overflow, invalid values, and other invocation parse/validation failures that represent customer input use the BAD_REQUEST family; genuine runtime failures retain their existing non-client classification.
These usage failures exit with code 1 in normal and quiet modes and do not start worker execution or other runtime side effects.
Focused CLI and process-boundary regression tests cover the reported unknown-argument reproduction and representative validation paths using the post-PR-#1859 test layout.
The authored you run error contract records the invocation client-error behavior and generated artifacts are refreshed with make cli-manifest-generate rather than edited manually.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented typed invocation-argument missing-value and static-flag parse errors, preserving existing stable ArgumentError codes and BAD_REQUEST classification. Added process-boundary coverage for the reported --planer-model typo in normal and quiet modes, dynamic/static missing values, positional overflow, and invalid JSON validation; all assert one stderr ErrorResponse, empty stdout, and zero provider calls. Updated authored CLI errors and regenerated family/published manifests with make cli-manifest-generate and make contracts-generate. Verification: focused Work/CLI packages, focused functional parameter/output tests, make cli-manifest-check, make typecheck, and git diff --check passed. The broad make test command reached its six-minute command timeout without emitting a test failure; no source failure was reported.

userStories.title: List accepted work and dependency edges
userStories.description: As an operator watching a run, I want to see the work admitted by a generated batch and how items depend on one another so that I understand the execution plan behind the count.
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-item work-accepted event renders the accepted count followed by one stable, readable entry for every canonical work item, including its ID/name and available task description without exposing private provider payloads.
Every canonical DEPENDS_ON relationship in the accepted batch is rendered once with an unambiguous source-to-prerequisite direction; independent items do not gain fabricated edges.
Single-item and empty or partially populated payloads remain readable and do not panic; absent optional descriptions or relations are omitted cleanly.
A deterministic recorded/golden rendering proves the item listing and dependency graph for a representative generated batch.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Show active workers and workstation work details
userStories.description: As an operator watching concurrent execution, I want one current state line per active worker and work-aware workstation transitions so that I can tell what is running and what completed.
acceptanceCriteria: Each concurrent active worker or dispatch has a distinct progress line that identifies its current state and remains associated with the same worker until a terminal outcome.
Workstation queued, started, completed, failed, and interrupted output names the workstation and includes canonical work IDs consumed or completed when the event provides them.
Terminal worker outcomes stop or replace the corresponding active indication without leaving stale workers displayed, including interleaved concurrent event sequences.
A deterministic recorded/golden run proves multiple simultaneous workers and their workstation/work associations without depending on timing sleeps.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Respect terminal policy while improving progress distinction
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want rich progress in an interactive terminal and clean deterministic output everywhere else so that the same command works for humans, logs, and automation.
acceptanceCriteria: In an eligible interactive non-JSON run, each active worker advances through the approved spinner frames and simultaneous workers receive visibly distinguishable colors from a varied, deterministic palette.
Progress rendering uses the existing terminal-policy decision for capabilities and channels; worker progress is sent to stderr and does not overwrite or contaminate the primary result on stdout.
Redirected or non-interactive human output uses stable status lines without cursor-control sequences, animation artifacts, or ANSI escapes, and --quiet suppresses progress.
JSON and NDJSON output remain parseable record-for-record and contain no spinner frames, ANSI escapes, or human-only workstation prose.
Existing unchanged CLI goldens remain unchanged; intentionally changed run goldens and CLI manifest artifacts are regenerated after the final rebase and each diff is explained in the PR.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
